# Calendar MVP Requirements Checklist: Simple Home Calendar MVP

**Purpose**: Validate that MVP calendar/task requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation changes.
**Created**: 2026-11-12
**Feature**: /home/richard/source/repos/WhatRWeDoinMrRobot/specs/001-calendar-task-agent/spec.md

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all required event attributes and constraints fully specified for create and edit flows (title, date, timed/all-day mode, details)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK002 Are persistence expectations explicitly defined for create, edit, and delete outcomes across refresh and restart scenarios? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012]

## Requirement Clarity

- [X] CHK003 Is "simple" in the interface requirement translated into concrete, testable UX acceptance language rather than subjective wording? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK004 Are validation-message requirements explicit enough to avoid inconsistent wording for required-title and invalid-time cases? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-013]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK005 Do user stories and functional requirements use consistent terminology for "event" versus "task" to prevent contract ambiguity? [Consistency, Conflict, Spec §User Stories, Spec §Functional Requirements]
- [x] CHK006 Are ordering requirements consistent across chronological sorting, all-day precedence, and tie-break behavior with no contradictory interpretation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006a, Spec §FR-006b, Spec §FR-006c]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK007 Can success criteria thresholds (time-to-create/edit and reflection rate) be objectively measured from written requirements without adding hidden assumptions? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK008 Are acceptance scenarios mapped to requirement IDs so each core behavior has traceable, measurable pass criteria? [Traceability, Gap]

## Scenario And Edge Coverage

- [x] CHK009 Are primary, alternate, and exception flows all specified for date selection, empty day state, save rejection, and unsaved-form exit? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK010 Are recovery expectations defined for failed save/update/delete operations (for example, retained form inputs and user guidance)? [Recovery, Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK011 Are non-functional requirements for accessibility and responsiveness explicitly stated for MVP interaction paths, not only implied by principle text? [Non-Functional, Gap, Constitution §I]

## Dependencies And Assumptions

- [x] CHK012 Is the intended MVP boundary (calendar/task only, excluding agent-related capability) explicitly reconciled across spec, plan, and task artifacts? [Scope, Assumption, Constitution §Delivery Constraints, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
